the auditor audits itself: the installed weekly line (crontab line 96) has no `cd /opt/fabrik`, so `.venv/bin/python` resolves against $HOME — its only scheduled attempt (2026-08-31) appended `not found` and 0 of 33 surfaces watched the watcher; it stays broken until the operator installs the script's own PROPOSED_CRON verbatim (review 2026-09-03, DA1). The marker is the stamped stderr line the audit prints on completion (a failed cron line appends only an error, never the marker); 180 h = a weekly run plus 12 h of late-cron slack — a MISSED Monday reads DEAD.

the external-services chain (scripts/external_services_chain.sh: gather_envs → classify → gather_envs → registry_sync → gen_dashboard), run by daily_refresh.sh and wsl_startup_hook.sh; the script stamps this file itself, ONLY after every DATA step (gather_envs, the second gather_envs — step label gather_envs_reconsolidate — and registry_sync) and the dashboard succeeded, via tmp + rename: a data step that fails, or a stamp it cannot write (alerted, exit 1), leaves the previous stamp to age past 30 h and read DEAD; the dashboard file's own mtime is NOT evidence — any manual gen_dashboard.py run refreshes it (review 2026-09-02, CY1/DA3); the paid classify step is deliberately NOT part of the heartbeat — its failure alerts but never ages the stamp (G9); the chain sat half-dead for 46 days before any surface named it
